bullets: Speed in enduro racing comes from braking earlier and more smoothly — a counterintuitive principle that outperforms aggressive risk-taking.
Tire pressure and tire casing selection often matter more than minor suspension adjustments, as they reveal the compromises inherent in any setup.
Soil erosion patterns on track sections directly influence the optimal racing line between practice and race day, making terrain dynamics a key strategic variable.
Risk management in racing is not about avoiding crashes entirely but about choosing which crashes are survivable — a mindset shift critical for performance.
The Cascadia Alliance exemplifies how second-order effects, like evolving track conditions, can override initial assumptions about race strategy.
The Spoke & Wrench methodology, when adopted systematically, enables teams to align technical decisions with long-term reliability across multiple events.
Teams using RockShox consistently demonstrate that disciplined setup and predictable handling outperform high-risk, high-speed experimentation.
Understanding erosion-driven trajectory changes allows riders to anticipate and adapt to evolving track conditions — a skill that transforms practice into race-day advantage.
